vocab.definition: two different electrodes in an electrolyte producing a voltage.
two or more cells connected together.
a metal that reacts to release or accept electrons.
a cell whose reaction can be reversed by electricity.

misconceptions.wrong: A single cell is a battery.
misconceptions.right: A battery is two or more cells joined.

misconceptions.wrong: Any two metals give the same voltage.
misconceptions.right: Voltage depends on the difference in reactivity.
Only some — non-rechargeable cells run out.

questions.text: State what is needed to make a simple cell produce a voltage. [2 marks]
Explain how to increase the voltage of a cell using the metals chosen. [2 marks]
State the difference between a cell and a battery. [1 mark]
Explain why a rechargeable cell can be used many times. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: A bigger difference in metal ______ gives a ______ voltage.

questions.text: Explain why a non-rechargeable cell eventually stops working. [1 mark]

footer.tip: Voltage depends on how far apart the two electrodes are in the reactivity series.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does a cell stop once one of the reactants is used up?
